editorial.headline: Industrial Combustion Engines, With a Bali Caveat
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28112 covers the manufacture of internal-combustion prime movers, nationally open to PMA but conditional in Bali by declared OSS scope.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28112 is the industrial engine code for makers of internal-combustion prime movers. In plain English, it covers the manufacture of engines that create motive power through combustion inside the engine itself: spark-ignition engines, compression-ignition engines such as diesel units, petrol engines, and engines using gas or alcohol fuels. The record also places industrial applications and piston internal-combustion engines inside the scope, including marine and railway engines, while keeping vehicle and aircraft engine manufacturing outside this activity. It also includes factory repair of ship and boat engines.

The scale profile is broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it is not framed as a code reserved only for large manufacturers. That said, the activity itself is industrial in character: the useful reading is not merely “engine trade”, but production of engine machinery and related factory repair. A founder choosing this code should be able to point from the declared activity to that manufacturing scope, not to a neighboring automotive or aircraft-engine line that the record expressly excludes.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling in the record is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is therefore a foreign-open activity with no lower percentage cap stated in the slim record. Nothing in the record adds a separate national condition, minimum capital number, tax rule, or special licence threshold, so none should be inferred from the code description alone.

Bali is more careful. The record does not mark the code as outright blocked for Bali, but it does mark the Bali status as Blocked (scope-dependent). The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity.” That sits beside the moratorium rule that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. The honest conclusion is that KBLI 28112 is nationally open, but in Bali it cannot be treated as automatically clean for every declared scope. The exact OSS activity and risk classification carry the decision.
editorial.pullQuote: KBLI 28112 is nationally open to foreign ownership, but in Bali the declared OSS scope determines whether the registration path is actually usable.
